summary: Floyd County, GA: a 100-ft wooden tower from 1938 replaced by a steel tower in 1957; the record ends 'Removed'; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 100-foot wooden lookout tower (1938 to 1957), replaced by a permanent steel structure
facts.status_note: The steel tower that replaced the wooden one is recorded as Removed, with no date; no source describes the site now

events.note: 100-foot wooden lookout tower, in service from 1938 per the 1957 article
manned by Joseph C. Lowery during the wooden tower's 19-year existence
Lowery retired at 82, 'last year' in the 1957 article; the same article says he was allowed to stay on to serve in the new tower
permanent steel structure replaced the wooden tower
wooden tower pulled from its foundation by two bulldozers
steel tower manned by Charles L. Evans, who was 21

evidence.supports: wooden tower, 100 feet, in service since 1938
evidence.quote: Since 1938, the 100-foot wooden sentinel stood guard over Floyd county

evidence.supports: tower overlooked the Hermitage community and was replaced by a steel structure
evidence.quote: the temporary wooden lookout tower that overlooked the once thriving Hermitage community has been replaced by a permanent steel structure

evidence.supports: Lowery manned the tower; started at 64
evidence.quote: During its 19-year existence, it was manned by Joseph C. Lowery, who started his lonely vigil at the age of 64.

evidence.supports: climbs of 120 steps three times a day
evidence.quote: climbed the 120 spiraling steps to the top of the tower three times a day
His daily climbs totaled an estimated 19,710 when he was retired last year at the age of 82.

evidence.supports: Lowery asked to remain on duty to serve in the new tower
evidence.quote: requested that he be allowed to remain on active duty long enough to serve in the new tower

evidence.supports: officials said instability was not the reason the tower was replaced
the tower was replaced for being the state's only remaining wooden lookout, not for instability
evidence.quote: it was replaced for that reason alone

evidence.supports: commission expected age to claim the sturdy beams in time
evidence.quote: it would be only a matter of time before age would claim the sturdy beams

evidence.supports: officials felt the tower's role in state fire protection was too vital to risk
evidence.quote: its role in the state's forest fire protection program was too vital

evidence.supports: Georgia Forestry Commission is the agency named in the record heading and text
only remaining wooden lookout tower in the state for over a year
evidence.quote: For more than a year it had the distinction of being the only remaining wooden lookout tower in the state

evidence.supports: two bulldozers pulled the old tower from its foundation
evidence.quote: It took two bulldozers almost half a day to tear the tower away from its foundation and pull it to the ground.

evidence.supports: steel tower manned by Charles L. Evans, age 21
evidence.quote: It is manned by Towerman Charles L. Evans who is only 21 years old.

sources.title: Hermitage - Forest Lookouts (reprints Rome News-Tribune article of June 21, 1957)

corrections.proposed: remove, or note that 30.5 m (100 ft) is the 1938 wooden tower's height; no source gives the steel tower's height
corrections.why: The 1957 article gives the 100-foot height for the wooden tower that the steel structure replaced

notes_for_editor: The 1957 article gives Lowery's retirement (last year, at 82) and also says he was allowed to stay on for the new tower; the story reports both without choosing. Steel tower height and date of its removal are not in any source; the only fate word is 'Removed'. Single 1957 newspaper article, reprinted on Forest Lookouts; original Rome News-Tribune not found. DLG Hermitage historical marker (dlg.usg.edu) concerns the settlement name, not the tower, so not used. A Savannah Morning News 2006 fire-tower article returned 403 and is not cited.
